candidates.title: Harden prototype AI workflows

demandEvidence.chore: Harden a prototype AI workflow with versioned logic, automated tests, and strict access controls.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: a workflow usually outgrows the prototype once it needs versioned logic, automated tests, strict access

ease.reason: A beginner can test one versioned workflow against synthetic inputs, but no supplied reference documents versioning or access controls.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent AI consultants may pay for workflow hardening; this discussion does not verify buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week demo could version one workflow and run a few tests; real systems, permissions and security review remain outside scope.

autonomy.reason: Proposed tests can run on each saved change, but a person must approve access rules and interpret failures; no implementation reference supports this.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly names versioned logic, automated tests and strict access as workflow needs, but gives no frequency or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: A proposed four-week experiment would version one synthetic workflow, run automated checks on fixed examples, and flag access settings for human review. Mean 23/5 = 4.6, below 6; no supplied building reference documents these capabilities.
